text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- U.S. threatens: We'll stop mediating peace process if Israel and Palestinians don't make mutual concessions during next Dennis Ross shuttle; U.S. sends message it mainly disappointed by Israel.
- Signing soon of huge arms deal between Russia and Syria to include MIG 29s.
- Search for submarine lost in 1960s resumes.
- Today attorney general discusses whether to defend Justice Minister continuing in his post in wake of prosecutors report which found insufficient evidence to charge him.
- MP Dalia Itzhik joins camp of Labour leader hopeful Barak.
- Father and baby die of auto accident injuries.
MAARIV

- Tension in Prime Minister Netanyahu's office after his declaration that there will be personnel changes; today composition of High Court panel to hear appeal that Netanyahu be charged over January attorney general appointment could be set.
- U.S. Secretary of State Albright calls Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to Washington.
- Woman, 25, who cannot give birth, sets self on fire.
- Twins, aged 4, weighing 40 kgs, die of obesity.
JERUSALEM POST
- Levy, Albright to meet Friday.
- Police seek public's help in Wadi Kelt terrorist probe.
- Moroccan Jewish Mimouna festival today.
HAARETZ
- Syria manufacturing new nerve gas and mounting it on warhead.
- Egypt's Mubarak plans four-way Arab summit including Syria's Assad, Jordan's King Hussein, and Palestinians' Arafat.
- U.S. could renew call to Germany to cancel loan to Iranian oil company.
- Army to add profile 30 to allow service without weapons.
- Funds to culture groups of ultra-Orthodox religious parties to increase.
- Ronen commission to present within week recommendations for construction bond offering.
- U.S. army will in 1998 stop acquisition contract with Telecom of Tadiran.
